workLog.action: Investigated the quality-gate downgrade path: it treated any final verdict in ATTENTION_VERDICTS (FAIL_VERDICTS | UNKNOWN | DID_NOT_RUN) as downgradeable to WARN whenever no non-infra CODE_QUALITY failure existed, without checking whether each individual infra-flagged verdict was actually an explicit infra-failure token.
workLog.result: Confirmed the gap: a literal UNKNOWN verdict or an unrecognized/raw token (e.g. a typo'd verdict string) on an infra-flagged axis would downgrade to WARN and pass the gate, even though neither token is a real infra-failure signal (only FAIL_VERDICTS and DID_NOT_RUN are).

workLog.action: Added is_blocking_unknown_verdict() and should_downgrade_infra_only_failures() to .github/scripts/aggregate_quality_verdicts.py, and replaced the blanket ATTENTION_VERDICTS downgrade check in main() with a per-agent verification that every failing verdict is an explicit member of DOWNGRADEABLE_INFRA_VERDICTS (FAIL_VERDICTS | DID_NOT_RUN) before allowing the WARN downgrade.
workLog.result: Literal UNKNOWN and unrecognized/raw verdict tokens on an infra-flagged axis now block should_downgrade_infra_only_failures() from returning True, so the gate can no longer be silently downgraded to WARN by those tokens.

workLog.action: Added regression tests test_unknown_infra_failure_stays_blocking and test_unrecognized_verdict_token_stays_blocking to tests/test_aggregate_quality_verdicts.py, pinning that DID_NOT_RUN plus a literal UNKNOWN (or plus an unrecognized token like FOOBAR) on infra-flagged axes still resolves to final_verdict UNKNOWN rather than WARN.
workLog.result: Ran the targeted pytest suite for tests/test_aggregate_quality_verdicts.py: all cases passed, including the two new regressions and the pre-existing infra downgrade cases. Committed as 84c76708c (fix(quality-gate): keep unknown verdicts blocking).
